Definition: from a compound of the base of G3674 and G3056; to assent, i.e. covenant, acknowledge:--con- (pro-)fess, confession is made, give thanks, promise.
BiblicalUsage: When Scripture says homologéō, it means to confess, to profess. The word appears 23 times, and in Matthew, Luke, John, and Acts it carries that same straightforward meaning. Nothing hidden sits behind it; the sense is the one you would expect from the word itself.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that homologéō matters because confession is not informing God of what He already knows — it is agreeing with Him. My position is simple: I take God at His word here, and I build on that.
